messages:
sara: quick alert — after last-night's envelope key rotation some prod requests are failing with KMS AccessDenied when trying to decrypt the data key. seen in multiple ECS tasks

josh: ugh. paste one of the exact errors and the key arn?

sara: error from app logs:
```
AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ecs-prod-task/abcd is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/aa11bb22-cc33-44dd-55ee-ff6677889900
```
Key id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/aa11bb22-cc33-44dd-55ee-ff6677889900

kms-bot: found CloudTrail entry for the failing calls — kms:Decrypt returned AccessDenied. Principal shows sts assumed-role ARN. EventTime: 2024-11-03T05:12:10Z.

paul: couple of quick checks: 1) key policy might not allow the assumed role principal, 2) permissions boundary or session policy could be denying kms:Decrypt, 3) any condition on the key (aws:PrincipalOrgID / aws:SourceAccount / aws:ViaService) that the assumed role doesn't match.

lina: also verify if we relied on a grant for cross-account or service usage — grants can be created for IAM principals and sometimes we created one-off grants for the rewrap job. list-grants on the key and see if the role is listed.

sara: ran these:
```
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id aa11bb22-cc33-44dd-55ee-ff6677889900 --policy-name default
```
policy shows only a couple admin principals and an org-scoped condition. no explicit entry for the ecs task role.

josh: paste the policy condition snippet — if there's an `aws:PrincipalOrgID` or `aws:SourceAccount` condition it may reject assumed-role ARNs from tasks that assume via STS in the same account but lack the org tag.

sara: policy snippet:
```
"Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:PrincipalOrgID": "o-1a2b3c4d" } }
```

paul: ok that's it. ECS assumed-role ARNs don't carry org id by default. When a principal is an assumed role the PrincipalOrgID condition often fails. Two options: 1) add the role ARN to key policy principals, 2) create a KMS grant for the role, or 3) loosen the org condition for decrypt action.

lina: quick repro: create a grant for the role so it can decrypt without changing policy. command: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ecs-prod-task --operations Decrypt`

josh: note: grants require the grantee to provide the GrantToken when using the grant immediately after creation if the call that needs it is in the same request chain; but for our long-lived tasks that isn't the case. Also grants survive key rotation but they are tied to the KMS key.

sara: I tried `aws kms list-grants --key-id ...` — output shows no grant for the ecs role. I can either add the role to the key policy or create a grant. Which is safer for prod?

paul: for service-to-service in same account, adding the role to the key policy is simplest and more auditable. For short-lived cross-account or third-party, prefer grants. Also confirm there is no permissions boundary blocking kms:Decrypt on the role.

sara: checked role's permissions boundary and session policy — nothing explicit blocking kms:Decrypt. IAM policy attached to role already has `"Action": "kms:Decrypt"` and `"Resource": "*"`. So it's definitely the key policy condition.

josh: recommended remediation: add a KeyPolicy statement allowing the specific role ARN with Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey and add a condition to restrict to the relevant VPC endpoints or source account if desired. then test.

sara: applied a temp key policy update to add the role principal. command used:
```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id aa11bb22-cc33-44dd-55ee-ff6677889900 --policy-name default --policy file://policy-with-ecs-role.json
```
policy change rolled out. re-ran failing job — decrypts succeeded. :tada:

lina: nice. followup tasks: 1) confirm no other services are implicitly blocked by the org condition, 2) create a small runbook documenting when to prefer grants vs policy edits, 3) add an alert for KMS AccessDenied spikes to catch this earlier.

sara: filing a one-pager and a Jira to update key policies for critical keys. will also check other keys that were rotated at the same time.

kms-bot: audit note — rotation job performed at 2024-11-03T00:10:02Z by automation-role. Created rotated data keys and pushed rotation record. No grants were modified by rotation.

josh: good catch. thanks for the quick triage and fix.

paul: also add a CloudTrail saved query for kms:Decrypt AccessDenied with "errorCode": "AccessDeniedException" and group by keyId/principal to speed future triage.

sara: will do. closing thread once I create the runbook + jira. :white_check_mark:
